hash_exempt.ResetVector: Raw reset-vector blob (SEC reset vector), not a PE/COFF image, so the GenFw --rebase 0 canonical-hash path does not apply. Explicit reviewed exemption for the component-integrity rule, not a silent pass. Reviewer: houdini91, 2026-08-02.

supported_hash_profiles._comment: Hash canonicalization profiles this verifier IMPLEMENTS, i.e. can re-derive from shipped bytes. A declared digest is comparable to a re-derived one ONLY when both used the same preimage transformation. Keyed by the value the SBOM carries in edk2:hashCanonicalForm. Spec: docs/normalized-module-hash-profile.md. An SBOM declaring a profile absent from this map is NOT comparable and the byte-integrity report fails and names it — rather than comparing digests over different preimages and calling the result a match or a tamper.
supported_hash_profiles.genfw-rebase-0: PE32/PE32+ normalized to ImageBase 0: base relocations reversed (HIGHLOW/DIR64), then ImageBase/TimeDateStamp/CheckSum zeroed as in-place byte patches. Implemented by producers/reconcile/ffs.py canon_unrebase(); conformance vectors in docs/normalized-module-hash-vectors.json (122 modules, 11 exercising the un-rebase).

byte_integrity_exempt._comment: Reviewed exemptions for the byte-integrity gate — {"ModuleName": "reason it genuinely cannot be byte-verified (e.g. a TE-only or compressed section) + reviewer + date"}. EMPTY today: the reference build byte-verifies all 122 PE-carrying modules. A module is added ONLY after human review; anything un-verifiable and NOT listed here fails the gate and is named.

binary_hardening_exempt._comment: Reviewed exemptions for the binary-hardening gate — {"ModuleName": "reason a DXE-class module genuinely cannot be scanned (e.g. a TE-only or compressed section) + reviewer + date"}. Only DXE-class modules that could NOT be scanned are eligible; a missing-NX finding is a regression and is NEVER exemptable. EMPTY today: the reference build scans all declared DXE-class modules. Added ONLY after human review; anything un-scannable and NOT listed here fails the gate and is named.

deploy_reconcile_exempt._comment: Reviewed exemptions for the deploy-time reconcile gate (Track A, CHIPSEC-fed) — {"ModuleName": "reason a declared module genuinely cannot be verified on the device (e.g. a legitimately TE-only or compressed on-device section CHIPSEC cannot extract to a normalizable PE) + reviewer + date"}. A MISMATCH / MISSING / UNEXPECTED module is on-device drift and is NEVER exemptable; only an UNVERIFIABLE (non-PE/TE skip or extraction error) declared module is eligible. EMPTY today: the OVMF reference reconciles all 122 PE-carrying modules. Added ONLY after human review; anything unverifiable and NOT listed here fails the gate and is named — a same-GUID PE->TE swap looks exactly like this.

kev_waivers._comment: Explicit EXEC-RISK VEX waivers for KEV findings — {"CVE-...": "why this KEV CVE is not exploitable in THIS firmware, with reviewer+date"}. This is SEPARATE from data.cve_allowlist: a plain not_affected there does NOT silence a KEV. A KEV entry is waived ONLY by a reviewed exec-risk justification here. EMPTY today.

evidence_grade._comment: Machine-readable strength grade per verifier report, emitted on each report as evidenceGrade so a green report is never read as an unqualified proof. verified = independently re-derived from the shipped bytes or a verified signature (measurement/crypto). declared = the SBOM/attestation asserts it; we check the claim is present + well-formed, not that it is true of the running firmware. sample = CHIPSEC-derived on a QEMU/OVMF target (config-level posture, NOT hardware-rooted silicon). This is the STATIC grade; firmware.rego DOWNGRADES a 'verified' report to 'assumed' whenever the assembler marks it in input.assumed_reports — i.e. a DEV_ASSUME_* leg stood in for the real check this run (offline demo). So the offline VSA shows slsa-provenance/slsa-level-floor/provenance-identity/signer-identity-pinned/build-tools-signed/evidence-chain-bound as 'assumed', matching the loud warnings; in CI (real keyless signature + platform provenance) assumed_reports is empty and these stay 'verified'. NOTE component-integrity is 'declared' (it checks every module CARRIES a declared hash — presence); the byte re-derivation is the separate component-byte-integrity report (verified). firmware-digest-anchor is 'declared' (self-asserted anchor; the real measurement is firmware-freshly-measured=verified).
